summary: Russian forces launched a massive coordinated drone assault across Ukraine overnight, with over 30 Shahed and reactive UAV groups targeting Kyiv, Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Kharkiv, Odesa, and other regions, resulting in a strike on the Novus shopping center in Vyshneve. Ukrainian air defenses engaged numerous targets, while search-and-rescue operations recovered a live child from Vyshneve rubble. On the ground, Ukrainian forces pushed back Russian troops near Ustynivka, though the enemy advanced near Verkhnya Tersa.
key_points: Russian forces launched Shahed and reactive UAVs from at least six airbases including Primorsko-Akhtarsk (10 groups), Orel, Millerovo, Gvardeyskoye, Shatalovo, and Kursk, targeting multiple Ukrainian regions simultaneously. (Source: @eRadarrua/132685)
A reactive Shahed struck the Novus shopping center in Vyshneve, Kyiv region, prompting search-and-rescue operations that extracted a live child from the rubble. (Source: @eRadarrua/132687)

Ukrainian unmanned surface vessels attacked and sank the Russian corvette Mercury near Libya, also damaging the sanctioned Russian roller ASCALON carrying military equipment. (Source: @UkraineNow/85466)
Ukrainian Defense Forces repelled Russian advances near Ustynivka in Donetsk region, while Russian troops progressed near Verkhnya Tersa. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24020)
Russian tactical aviation conducted guided aerial bomb strikes on Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions. (Source: @kpszsu/98530)
Slovak Prime Minister Fico announced Slovakia will not join the new €45 billion EU loan for Ukraine, calling it a politically pressured gift Ukraine cannot repay. (Source: @UkraineNow/85457)
Czech Prime Minister Babiš threatened to block the proposed €100 billion EU aid package for Ukraine, deeming the EU budget unacceptable. (Source: @UkraineNow/85461)
Russian Rosgvardia Colonel General Aleksandr Poryadin died; Ukrainian HUR attributes him to punitive operations against civilians in occupied territories. (Source: @UkraineNow/85465)

sections.executive_summary: Russian forces launched a massive coordinated drone assault across Ukraine overnight, with over 30 Shahed and reactive UAV groups targeting Kyiv, Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Kharkiv, Odesa, and other regions, resulting in a strike on the Novus shopping center in Vyshneve. Ukrainian air defenses engaged numerous targets, while search-and-rescue operations recovered a live child from Vyshneve rubble. On the ground, Ukrainian forces pushed back Russian troops near Ustynivka, though the enemy advanced near Verkhnya Tersa.

points: Ukrainian unmanned surface vessels conducted a successful attack on the Russian corvette Mercury near the Libyan coast, sinking the vessel and damaging the sanctioned Russian roller ASCALON which was transporting military equipment including BMPs and BTRs from Baltiysk. (Source: @UkraineNow/85466, @UkraineNow/85467)
Ukrainian Defense Forces pushed back Russian troops near Ustynivka in Donetsk region, demonstrating continued effective local counterattacks despite pressure elsewhere. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24020)

Search-and-rescue teams in Vyshneve, Kyiv region, extracted a live child from the rubble of the Novus shopping center following a reactive Shahed strike, while recovering four bodies with ten people still unaccounted for. (Source: @eRadarrua/132687, @UkraineNow/85468)

Ukrainian air defense units engaged multiple waves of Shahed and reactive UAVs across at least ten oblasts, with monitoring channels reporting interceptions and tracking of drones over Kyiv, Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Kharkiv, Odesa, and other regions. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78725, @eRadarrua/132677)
Rescue operations continued in Dymer, Kyiv region, where a five-story building was destroyed, with rescuers recovering bodies from the rubble throughout the day. (Source: @UkraineNow/85458)

Russian forces launched Shahed and reactive UAVs from six identified airbases: Primorsko-Akhtarsk (10 groups), Orel (5+2 groups reactive), Millerovo (2+2 groups reactive), Gvardeyskoye (2+3 groups reactive), Shatalovo (2+2 groups), and Kursk (5+6 groups), indicating a large-scale coordinated strike package. (Source: @eRadarrua/132685, @eRadarrua/132691, @eRadarrua/132681, @eRadarrua/132698)

Russian tactical aviation employed guided aerial bombs against Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions, continuing the campaign of stand-off strikes against Ukrainian rear areas. (Source: @kpszsu/98530, @kpszsu/98547)

Russian Rosgvardia Colonel General Aleksandr Poryadin was confirmed dead; Ukrainian military intelligence (HUR) states he was involved in punitive operations against civilians in temporarily occupied territories. (Source: @UkraineNow/85465)

Russian air defense claims of repelling a second USV attack on the corvette Mercury near Libya were contradicted by video evidence showing the vessel sinking after Ukrainian unmanned surface vessel strikes. (Source: @UkraineNow/85466)

Russian forces advanced near Verkhnya Tersa in Donetsk region while being pushed back near Ustynivka, indicating ongoing grinding attritional combat along the eastern front. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24020)
Ukrainian forces repelled Russian advances near Ustynivka in Donetsk region, a localized tactical success amid broader pressure. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24020)
Russian troops made gains near Verkhnya Tersa in Donetsk region, continuing incremental advances in the sector. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24020)
A reactive UAV launched from Donetsk region flew toward Dnipropetrovsk region, targeting the Pavlohrad area, demonstrating cross-front drone employment. (Source: @eRadarrua/132695)
Russian guided aerial bomb strikes hit Dnipropetrovsk region, likely targeting logistics or infrastructure behind the front lines. (Source: @kpszsu/98530)

Reactive UAVs were observed over Kharkiv city and near Krasnokutsk, Bogodukhiv, Vilshana, Staryi Merchyk, and Pechenihy, indicating persistent aerial reconnaissance and strike activity along the northeastern front. (Source: @kpszsu/98529, @kpszsu/98546, @eRadarrua/132689, @eRadarrua/132690, @eRadarrua/132693, @eRadarrua/132697)

Multiple Geran-5 missiles and reactive Shaheds were launched from Chernihiv region toward Kyiv region (Vyshhorod district) and from Zhytomyr region toward Rivne region (Sarny district), with at least three Geran-5s and one reactive Shahed tracked on each vector. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78725)
A reactive UAV from Chernihiv region flew past Snovsk heading south, while another from Zhytomyr region (Narodychi area) moved toward Kyiv region. (Source: @kpszsu/98521, @eRadarrua/132645)

Kyiv region air defenses engaged reactive UAVs near Ivankiv, Krasiatychi, Tetiyiv, Pereiaslav-Khmelnytskyi, and Slavutych, with the air raid alert lifted at 18:37 on 22 November 2026. (Source: @kpszsu/98524, @kpszsu/98526, @eRadarrua/132643, @eRadarrua/132682)

A Geran-5 missile struck Vyshneve/Chabany in Kyiv region, and a reactive Shahed hit the Novus shopping center in Vyshneve, causing casualties and structural collapse. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78726, @UkraineNow/85462, @eRadarrua/132683)

Reactive UAVs from Sumy region flew past Trostianets heading north and past Novyi Sanzhary toward Poltava region, while a reactive UAV from Poltava region (Karlivka area) moved toward Poltava city. (Source: @kpszsu/98536, @kpszsu/98523, @kpszsu/98528)

Strike UAVs launched from the Black Sea targeted Odesa and Lyman areas, while reactive UAVs from the Black Sea headed toward the Tuzlovski Lymany national park and Mykolaiv region (Ochakiv). (Source: @kpszsu/98560, @kpszsu/98532, @kpszsu/98550)

Reactive UAVs in southern Odesa region moved toward Kiliia, and a reactive UAV from Odesa region flew toward Vinnytsia region (Haisyn district) via Liubashivka. (Source: @kpszsu/98534, @eRadarrua/132695)
A reactive UAV near Berezanka in Mykolaiv region flew on a northwesterly course, and Mykolaiv region reported four groups of reactive UAVs active. (Source: @kpszsu/98553, @eRadarrua/132642)

Ukrainian unmanned surface vessels attacked Russian naval assets near Libya, sinking the corvette Mercury and damaging the roller ASCALON carrying military equipment, extending Ukrainian reach far beyond the Black Sea. (Source: @UkraineNow/85466, @UkraineNow/85467)
Reactive UAVs from Dnipropetrovsk region targeted Kirovohrad region (Oleksandriia district) and Zaporizhzhia region reported one reactive UAV group. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78725, @eRadarrua/132642)

Russian forces launched a massive wave of Shahed and reactive UAVs from at least six airbases: Primorsko-Akhtarsk (10 groups), Orel (7 groups reactive), Millerovo (4 groups reactive), Gvardeyskoye (5 groups reactive), Shatalovo (4 groups), and Kursk (11 groups), totaling over 40 launch groups in a single night. (Source: @eRadarrua/132685, @eRadarrua/132691, @eRadarrua/132681, @eRadarrua/132698)

Reactive Shaheds and Geran-5 missiles were tracked across at least 12 Ukrainian oblasts: Kyiv, Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk, Kharkiv, Odesa, Mykolaiv, Cherkasy, Kirovohrad, Poltava, Sumy, Chernihiv, Zhytomyr, and Rivne, with multiple simultaneous vectors. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78725, @eRadarrua/132677, @eRadarrua/132667)
A reactive Shahed flying at 4,000 meters altitude and 555 km/h was tracked over Vyshhorod toward Troieshchyna in Kyiv region, indicating high-performance drone variants. (Source: @mon1tor_ua/78723)

Russian tactical aviation conducted guided aerial bomb strikes on Dnipropetrovsk and Zaporizhzhia regions, complementing the drone campaign with stand-off precision munitions. (Source: @kpszsu/98530, @kpszsu/98547)

Ukrainian air defense monitoring reported reactive UAVs near Slavutych and Cherkasy region after the main wave, with Kyiv region declared clear at 18:37 on 22 November 2026. (Source: @eRadarrua/132670, @eRadarrua/132682)

Slovakia (PM Fico) and Czechia (PM Babiš) opposed new EU financial packages for Ukraine (€45bn loan and €100bn aid), citing political pressure and budget concerns, threatening EU unity on Ukraine support. (Source: @UkraineNow/85457, @UkraineNow/85461)

sections.threat_assessment: The scale and coordination of the 22-23 November drone wave — over 40 launch groups from six Russian airbases targeting 12+ Ukrainian regions — indicates a sustained Russian capacity for massed stand-off strikes despite Ukrainian air defense improvements. The use of high-speed reactive Shaheds (555 km/h at 4,000m) alongside Geran-5 missiles complicates interception timelines. The strike on civilian infrastructure in Vyshneve and the ongoing rescue operations highlight the persistent threat to rear areas. On the ground, the seesaw near Ustynivka/Verkhnya Tersa suggests neither side has decisive tactical advantage in eastern Donetsk. The Ukrainian USV success near Libya demonstrates an expanding asymmetric maritime threat to Russian logistics far from the Black Sea, potentially forcing Russian naval redeployments. Political fragmentation in EU aid (Slovakia, Czechia) poses a medium-term strategic risk to Ukrainian sustainment.
sections.regional_response: Slovak Prime Minister Fico's refusal to join the €45 billion EU loan and Czech Prime Minister Babiš's threat to block the €100 billion aid package reveal growing fractures in EU consensus on Ukraine funding, with both leaders framing assistance as politically coerced and financially unsustainable. Hungary's alignment with this stance (implied by Visegrad Four coordination) could paralyze EU-level financial mechanisms. Meanwhile, Finland's pursuit of €25+ billion in arbitration awards against Gazprom signals a parallel economic pressure track. Cyprus's expulsion of two Russian diplomats for GRU espionage targeting EU-sanctioned technology transfers reflects broader European counterintelligence pushback. These developments collectively indicate a shifting European landscape where military aid continuity is increasingly contested domestically.
